Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GreenWave Renewables Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for those joining by phone will follow shortly. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GreenWave Renewables' results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; and Taylor Kim, Chief Development Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. GreenWave Renewables delivered a solid performance in the third quarter, driven by strong execution and growing demand for our renewable energy solutions. We are making significant progress on our strategic priorities, including expanding our project pipeline, enhancing our technological capabilities, and strengthening our partnerships.

I'd like to highlight four key aspects of our performance this quarter. First, our development pipeline saw record additions and we hit major project milestones that advance our growth trajectory. Second, we navigated favorable PPA pricing trends while securing valuable contract extensions to bolster long-term visibility. Third, our gross and operating margins continued to expand, reflecting operational efficiencies and a favorable revenue mix. And fourth, our financing strategy, including tax equity and project-level deals, unlocked substantial capital to fuel expansion.

Let me start with the pipeline and milestones, which remain the foundation of our multi-year growth. In Q3, we added a record 4.2 GW to our global development pipeline, bringing our total owned and controlled capacity to 28.6 GW across solar PV, onshore wind, battery energy storage systems, and green hydrogen projects. This marks a 28% increase quarter-over-quarter and 45% year-over-year, outpacing industry peers. Our focus is on high-irradiance sites, hybrid configurations stacking multiple revenue streams, and long-term PPAs with investment-grade buyers.

By technology, utility-scale solar PV led with 2.8 GW added, highlighted by the 1.2 GW Vista del Sol portfolio in Arizona and Nevada, utilizing First Solar's thin-film CdTe modules for optimal performance in challenging conditions. These secure a 30% ITC adder for domestic content, targeting 12-14% unlevered IRRs, backed by 15-year PPAs with Amazon Web Services. Onshore wind contributed 1.0 GW, including the 450 MW Prairie Winds III in Oklahoma with GE Vernova's advanced turbines delivering 15% capacity factor gains for ERCOT ancillary services. BESS and hybrids added 400 MW/1.6 GWh, such as the Rattlesnake Solar + Storage in California with Tesla Megapack units for CAISO frequency regulation—hybrids now 35% of the pipeline as LCOE drops below $25/MWh. We also advanced 50 MW green hydrogen pilots with Plug Power, eyeing DOE hydrogen hubs.

Regionally, North America dominates at 75% or 21.5 GW, with strong queue positions in SPP, MISO, and ERCOT. Latin America gained 1.5 GW in Chile's Atacama for high-IRR PPAs tied to mining decarbonization, and Europe added 500 MW in Poland under REPowerEU, despite grid challenges.

On milestones, we achieved 10 key advancements for 3.1 GW. We reached FID on Desert Bloom I & II, 850 MW in Texas, with $1.2 billion financing from JPMorgan and Allianz, COD in Q4 2025. NTP issued for Horizon Wind Farm, 320 MW in Iowa, 20% constructed. First energy at SunForge Storage, 200 MW/800 MWh in Arizona, at 98.5% availability, unlocking $45 million ITCs. We signed 2.2 GW in PPAs, including Microsoft for 500 MW and PG&E for 700 MW at blended $28/MWh. Plus, 1.8 GW advanced permitting in PJM. This builds a $15.2 billion backlog, 8x forward EBITDA, with 1 GW for data center behind-the-meter power and AI yield optimization adding 200 bps to economics.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to discuss our financial results in more detail, including PPA trends, financing, and margin performance.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong financial performance in Q3. Our revenue was $1.2 billion, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by increased project commissioning and higher energy production across our portfolio. Our gross margin was 28.7%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $175 million, primarily due to increased investments in research and development and sales and marketing. Our net income was $120 million, or $1.55 per share. We ended the quarter with $950 million in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Building on Alex's points, let me dive deeper into PPA pricing trends and contract extensions, which account for 92% of our expected adjusted EBITDA through 2030. We've executed over 15 GW of PPAs since inception, averaging 15-year tenors. Post-2022, PPA pricing has stabilized and rebounded after the 2018-2021 oversupply. Globally, new solar PPAs rose 8-12% YoY in 2024 to $28/MWh in the US from $24/MWh, per NREL—driven by EPC inflation like 20% polysilicon spikes, higher rates compressing IRRs to 6-8% needing 1.5x DSCR, and storage premiums where solar-plus-4H BESS hits $45-55/MWh.

In the US, ERCOT leads: our 500 MW Rattlesnake Solar locked a 12-year PPA at $32/MWh with shape-flex pricing for hyperscaler demand. CAISO softer at $26/MWh, but our 300 MW Central Valley bifacial with trackers hit 28% capacity factor for $29/MWh. Europe: German EEG at €45/MWh ($49/MWh), UK CfD AR6 at £47/MWh for our Moray Firth extensions. APAC: Australia NEM at AUD 55/MWh ($36/MWh), India SECI at INR 2.5/kWh but shifting to C&I with Reliance.

Technologically, N-type TOPCon from First Solar/Longi at 22.5% efficiency cuts LCOE 5-7%, paired with Array trackers and Fluence BESS for 10-15% below-market bids on 20-year terms. Our AI PPA optimizer structures collars capturing 70% merchant upside in PJM.

On extensions, we announced 2.3 GW across our 8 GW fleet, adding $1.2 billion backlog at $34/MWh—15% premium. Wind Horizon 450 MW repowered with Vestas V150-15MW to 45% capacity factor, extended with Xcel to 2040 at $38/MWh, 12% IRR. Only 8% merchant now, with Amazon 1 GW inflation-linked, IRA 45Z for hydrogen, REPowerEU subsidies. Expect 5-10% firmer pricing in 2025 on data center loads; 20 GW pipeline 65% contracted, 70% hybrid for 15-18% FCF CAGR, 9-11% ROIC.

Next, tax equity financing and project-level financing have scaled our 5.2 GW operating and 12 GW development pipelines. Tax equity monetizes ITC at 30%+10% adders and PTC $27/MWh. Q3 closed $650 million for Desert Bloom 450 MW Arizona solar-plus-storage and Texas/California portfolios with U.S. Bancorp/KeyState at 8-10% flips. Investors get 99% allocations pre-flip at 8.5% hurdle, then 5% yield. Our pricing at 9.2% IRR. IRA 6418 transfers monetized $120 million ITCs at 95-98 cents to Google, cutting tax equity reliance to 45%. Project $2.1 billion FY25 for 3 GW, 38% effective ITC with First Solar.

US leads at $25 billion industry 2023; Europe green bonds with Allianz in Spain; Asia ADB debt. Project financing: $1.2 billion Q3 at 5.8% blended non-recourse. $400 million construction at SOFR+175 bps via MUFG/ING, mini-perms to 15-20 year term at SOFR+140 bps, $300 million Arizona at 5.2% fixed swaps. Green debt $550 billion 2023, 60% DSCR P90, SCADA-tied, ESG margins. Portfolio $800 million green bond for seven projects at 4.9%. Australia CEFC for Queensland BESS. Mix: 45% tax equity, 40% debt, 15% equity for 12-14% IRRs. Targeting $4.5 billion FY25 at 6% capital cost.

Finally, gross and operating margins showcase our integrated model. Q3 GAAP gross margin 28.7%, +340 bps YoY to 25.3%, non-GAAP 29.2%; TTM 27.8%, high-end peers. Revenue mix: EPC/O&M 22% at 35% margins offsets module ASP drop to $0.24/W. COGS: polysilicon $8.5/kg -40% YoY, silver $22/oz, Arizona fab 85% utilization cuts Xinjiang reliance 70%. US 65% gross profit via ITC safe-harbor; Europe 18% subsidy delays; APAC tariffs passed through. Q4 to 30%+ on 80% TOPCon CTM 96.5%, Ohio gigafactory.

OpCo margin GAAP 14.2%, +280 bps YoY; non-GAAP 15.1%; TTM 13.9%. OpEx 14.5% revenue despite $18 million incremental: SG&A 7.2%, R&D 4.8% ($58 million) on HJT-perovskite and CATL LFP BESS. Fortress America unlocks 500 bps via domestic bonuses; AI O&M at 0.4% degradation adds 200 bps. FY24 14.5%, FY25 16-18% on hybrids at 32% gross.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Alex for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Jordan. In closing, I am confident that GreenWave Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for queuing questions. Our first question comes from Mike Harlan with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Harlan:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of your new hybrid solar-plus-storage systems on your project economics?

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, Mike. Absolutely, our hybrid solar-plus-storage projects are transforming economics across the board. As Jordan touched on, these configurations command 60% premiums, with PPAs at $45-55/MWh versus standalone solar, thanks to 4-hour BESS enabling dispatchable power for data centers and grids. In our pipeline, hybrids are 35% and rising, dropping LCOE below $25/MWh while stacking ancillary revenues—like $50/kW-month in ERCOT. For instance, Rattlesnake delivers 12-14% IRRs with 60% DSCR at P90 yields, bolstered by Fluence and Tesla integrations. This not only de-risks offtake but captures merchant upside via AI-optimized collars, adding 200 bps to returns. We're seeing this play out in recent FIDs like Desert Bloom, where storage unlocks higher capacity factors and IRA adders. Happy to follow up offline.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What are your expectations for grid connection timelines for your upcoming projects?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Lisa. Grid timelines remain a key focus, but our proactive queue management positions us well. For our 21.5 GW North American pipeline, over 10 GW holds interconnection agreements in ERCOT, SPP, and MISO. Recent cluster approvals advanced 1.8 GW in PJM, and we're mitigating delays with co-location strategies—hybrids reduce individual queue risks. In Q4, expect NTPs on 2 GW, with CODs staggered through 2026: Texas FIDs like Desert Bloom on track for Q4 2025 despite ERCOT congestion, aided by merchant flexibility. Europe Poland additions face bottlenecks but leverage REPowerEU fast-tracks. Overall, 60% contracted mitigates delays, with forward supply secures for polysilicon and trackers. We're ahead of peers, targeting 25-30% FFO growth.

Operator:
Instructions confirmed. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for any closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in GreenWave Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
